title: The Prompt Is an Architecture: Spectral Species Taxonomy at the Instruction Level
summary: The prompt is conventionally treated as input to a fixed computational architecture. We show this framing inverts the relative magnitudes: across five model configurations, prompt-induced variation in spectral geometry (75.9% of mean sigma_1/sigma_2) exceeds architecture-induced variation at matched prompt levels (41.7%). Using singular value decomposition of hidden-state representations under identity-loading interventions (CCS), we demonstrate that instruction-level parameters produce the same spectral species taxonomy as model-level architecture parameters.
